subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The remaining work changes user-visible failure delivery and config surface; it improves hosted chat UX but can also hide failed mutations that current policy intentionally surfaces.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep boolean suppression only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this request to docs or channel-specific bugs.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle specific remaining leaks such as Feishu, exec-like warnings, or lifecycle routing in their own issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged warning-policy PR explicitly separated this issue as the broader delivery-policy decision.
